textbookText: During this type of life cycle, two haploid somatic cells unite to form diploid zygote. Zygote also behaves as diploid somatic cell and multiplies by budding to produce number of diploid somatic cells. Each of the diploid somatic cell behaves as ascus, nucleus of which divides meiotically to produce four haploid nuclei. Each of these nuclei organizes into ascospores. Ascospores, on liberation from ascus multiply by budding and produce haploid somatic cells.

2.2.5 INTRODUCTION OF MUSHROOM Mushroom is saprophytic fungus grow on damp and dead organic substances such as humus, animal dung, damp rotten logs of wood, trunks of trees and meadows rich in decaying organic matter. The mushrooms are commonly seen growing on grasslands and other places rich in humus soil during rainy season.
The body of mushroom is divided into two main parts: 1. Mycelium or vegetative body 2. Basidiocarp or fruiting body
1. Mycelium or vegetative body: It is comprised of profusely branched thread like
structure known as hyphae growing in the substratum. It remains hidden under the soil. The network of hyphae forms the mycelium and fruiting body.
Figure 2.4.16 Structure of mushroom

2. Basidiocarp or fruiting body: The fruiting body consists of a fleshy cylindrical stalk, known as stipe and an umbrella like head or cap called pileus. Stipe and pileus are made of interwoven mass of hyphae. During young stage, the fructification is the rounded and covered by thin membranous covering called velum. After growth of pileus, the velum is ruptured and remains attached to the stripe in the form of ring, called annulus. On the lower surface of the pileus, there is a large number of thin, vertical, plates like structures called gills or lamellae. It is the reproductive part which produces spores.

2.2.6 ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE OF FUNGI Fungi have both useful and harmful effects in our daily life.

Useful Effects: 1. Medicinal value: Different types of fungi are used in the production of numbers of drugs. Penicillin, claviformin and other antibiotic are extracted from Penicillium species. Vitamin B-complex, vitamin A and vitamin B-12 are obtained from Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Eremothemium ashbyii respectively. Different types of steroids are also synthesized from fungi.

2. Food value: Fungi are used as food by humans from a long time ago. The fruiting bodies of mushroom are used as food due to their high protein content and have good amount of vitamins, minerals and very less amount of fat.
Biology, Grade 11 | 100

3. Industrial value: Fungi are used in the production of different types of commercially important products such as alcoholic products (using yeast like, Saccharomyces, Rhizopus, Penicillium etc), bakery products (using yeast), Cheese (using Penicillium species), enzymes (like, amylase, cellulose, invertase etc.) and other organic acids (like; citric acid, fumaric acid, lactic acid, oxalic acid, etc).

4. Soil fertility: Decomposition of litter and wood in the forest takes place by the different types of fungi. Fungi like Fusarium, Chaetomium, Aspergillus, etc can decompose the structural polymers such as cellulose, hemicellulose, lipid, protein, starch etc. By decomposing the organic matters, fungi help to increase minerals and other substances in the soil, hence the fertility of soil increases.
5. Plant Nutrition: The mycorrhizal association of fungi and root of higher plants help in absorption of water and minerals.
6. Production of plant hormone: Some soil funguses are used to produce plant hormone like Gibberellin.

7. Biological control: Some fungi are used to control plant diseases in sustainable disease management systems. Beauveria bassiana is a naturally occurring fungus in soil has been use for control of soil borne insects like beetle etc.
